messages.subject: CFA vs Invariance of a test different CFI
parts:
Hi,

This is a cross post from stackoverflow as I'm not getting much luck there. Please delete if its not appropriate

I am currently learning how to implement CFA and invariance of constructs between two groups. My data below has two groups. So my steps are as follows

 - Confirm the overall model works
 - Check if both groups have a high enough `CFI`to perform `invariance` testing
 - Perform invariance testing (Configural, Metric, Scalar etc)

I originally created a CFA on a model and got a `CFI` of 0.9305597.
When I attempted to implement `invariance` testing the `configural` step gave me a `CFI` of 0.9233984

    model.between.groups <- measurementInvariance(model=HS.model, data = mydf, group="school", strict = TRUE)

For the `configural` step I got a value of 0.90 for the `CFI`

My understanding of the the `configural` step is that it just combines the groups together with no restrictions on the model. I'm basing this on my readings of [1][2]. I could be picking up the wrong end of the stick completely though

Should the `CFI` not be the same as when im combining the two groups together to test for invariance?

Below is a reproducible example which you should be able to run if the `lavaan` library is installed (I apologize for the spaghetti code) The table `fit_df` contains the fit statistics

Any suggestions or help to help me wrap my head around this would be great

Thanks for your time

1 - Confirmatory Factor Analysis for Applied Research - T Brown
2 - Latent Variable Modeling Using R - Beaujean, Alexander

Code

    library(lavaan)
    library(tidyverse)

    # Function to find the CFA fit put into a Table
    find_cfa_fit <- function(model, group, construct) {
 
      rmsea = paste(round(fitmeasures(model, 'rmsea')[[1]],4),
                " CI = [",round(fitmeasures(model,'rmsea.ci.lower', 'rmsea')[[1]],4),"-",
                round(fitmeasures(model,'rmsea.ci.upper')[[1]],4),
                "] p = ",round(fitmeasures(model,'rmsea.pvalue')[[1]],4), sep = '')
      srmr = fitmeasures(model, 'srmr')[[1]]
      cfi = fitmeasures(model, 'cfi')[[1]]
      tli = fitmeasures(model, 'tli')[[1]]
      chi_squared = as.numeric(fitmeasures(model,'chisq'))
 
      return(data.frame(construct, group,rmsea,srmr,cfi,tli,chi_squared))
 
    }

    mydf <- HolzingerSwineford1939

    # First Create the CFA model for both groups combined
    HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
    textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
    speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9 '

    # Fitting the model with both groups together
    all.fit <- cfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939)
    summary(fit_all, standardized= TRUE, rsquare = TRUE)

    # Create a table of fit statistics
    fit_df <- data.frame(construct = 'HSM',
                     group = 'All',
                     rmsea = paste(round(fitmeasures(all.fit, 'rmsea')[[1]],4),
                                   " CI = [",round(fitmeasures(all.fit,'rmsea.ci.lower', 'rmsea')[[1]],4),"-",
                                   round(fitmeasures(all.fit,'rmsea.ci.upper')[[1]],4),
                                   "] p = ",round(fitmeasures(all.fit,'rmsea.pvalue')[[1]],4), sep = ''),
                     srmr = fitmeasures(all.fit, 'srmr')[[1]],
                     cfi = fitmeasures(all.fit, 'cfi')[[1]],
                     tli = fitmeasures(all.fit, 'tli')[[1]],
                     chi_squared = fitmeasures(all.fit,'chisq'))


    # Split by Group to check that CFI is high enough for both groups to do invariant testing
    construct.pasteur <- filter(mydf, school == 'Pasteur')
    construct.gw <- filter(mydf, school == 'Grant-White')

    pasteur.fit <- cfa(HS.model, data = construct.pasteur, meanstructure = TRUE)
    gw.fit <- cfa(HS.model, data = construct.gw, meanstructure = TRUE)

    # Specify the fit values
    fit_df <- fit_df %>%
      rbind (find_cfa_fit(pasteur.fit,'pasteur', construct = 'HSM')) %>%
      rbind (find_cfa_fit(gw.fit,'gw', construct = 'HSM'))

    # Remove the Row Names
    row.names(fit_df) <- NULL

    # Model Invariance to see if its possible to use the questionaire across groups
    model.between.groups <- measurementInvariance(model=HS.model, data = mydf, group="school", strict = TRUE)

    # Add the model statistics to the summary Table
    fit_df <-  fit_df %>%
      rbind (find_cfa_fit(model.between.groups$fit.configural,'All', construct = 'Configural')) %>%
      rbind (find_cfa_fit(model.between.groups$fit.loadings,'All', construct = 'Metric')) %>%
      rbind (find_cfa_fit(model.between.groups$fit.intercepts,'All', construct = 'Scaler')) %>%
      rbind (find_cfa_fit(model.between.groups$fit.residuals,'All', construct = 'Strict'))

    # Retrieve the difference between CFI
    fit_df$diff[5:7] <- head(fit_df[4:nrow(fit_df), 5] - c(fit_df[5:(nrow(fit_df)), 5],0),3)

Comparing degrees of freedom may be a better way to compare models. If degrees of freedom are different, then you know the models are not the same.
     A configural invariance model should yield a chi-square and DF that are simple sums of the chi-squares and DFs for the separate group models. If you get something else, then something has changed. It might be easier to determine what has changed if we could see more of your syntax and output.

Hi

I have a much simpler example now where the degrees of freedom basically double because the configural test treats them as two groups
My understanding of this step was that it just pushed the two groups together without any restrictions i.e. it just checked if the CFA was good enough before exploring groups
Is this not the case. Thank you very much for your time and patience

# OLD LAVAAN METHOD -----------------------

library(lavaan)
library(tidyverse)

mydf <- HolzingerSwineford1939

# First Create the CFA model for both groups combined
HS.model <- ' visual  =~ x1 + x2 + x3
textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
speed   =~ x7 + x8 + x9'

# Fitting the CFA Model irespective of groups
all.fit <- cfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939)
summary(all.fit, standardized= TRUE, rsquare = TRUE)

# Fitting the CFA by Merging the groups
configural.fit <- cfa(HS.model, data=HolzingerSwineford1939, meanstructure = TRUE, group="school")
summary(configural.fit, standardized= TRUE, rsquare = TRUE)

# Create Fit Indices
fit.indices <- c('chisq','df','cfi','tli','srmr','rmsea','rmsea.ci.lower','rmsea.ci.upper')

fit_df <- as.data.frame(fitmeasures(object = all.fit, fit.indices)) %>%
  cbind(as.data.frame(fitmeasures(object = configural.fit, fit.indices)))

names(fit_df) <- c('CFA_Model','config.fit')

View(fit_df)

    # Model Invariance to see if its possible to use the questionaire across groups
    model.between.groups <- measurementInvariance(model=HS.model, data = mydf, group="school", strict = TRUE)

    # Add the model statistics to the summary Table
    fit_df <-  fit_df %>%
      rbind (find_cfa_fit(model.between.groups$fit.configural,'All', construct = 'Configural')) %>%
      rbind (find_cfa_fit(model.between.groups$fit.loadings,'All', construct = 'Metric')) %>%
      rbind (find_cfa_fit(model.between.groups$fit.intercepts,'All', construct = 'Scaler')) %>%
      rbind (find_cfa_fit(model.between.groups$fit.residuals,'All', construct = 'Strict'))

    # Retrieve the difference between CFI
    fit_df$diff[5:7] <- head(fit_df[4:nrow(fit_df), 5] - c(fit_df[5:(nrow(fit_df)), 5],0),3)

messages.subject: Re: CFA vs Invariance of a test different CFI
parts:
My understanding of this step was that it just pushed the two groups together without any restrictions i.e. it just checked if the CFA was good enough before exploring groups. Is this not the case?

The difference between a single-group and multigroup model is the input data.  If you constrain all parameters in a 2-group model to be equal across groups, that should result in identical parameter estimates as the single-group model.  But the 2-group model will result in 2 model-implied covariance matrices (one per group), which are compared to 2 observed covariance matrices used as input.  By contrast, a single-group model will only result in a single model-implied covariance matrix, compared to a single (pooled) observed covariance matrix.  Because that is what fit measures are based on, the df will be larger in the multigroup model because you estimate the same number of parameters but you have twice as much input information.

So to answer your original question "Should the `CFI` not be the same as when im combining the two groups together to test for invariance?", unless your model fits perfectly to both groups, there is no guarantee of finding consistent fit indices between a single-group model fit to the pooled sample or to individual groups, a 2-group model with no across-group constraints (configural model), and a 2-group model with all across-group constraints.  When your model fits only approximately well (or poorly), patterns of inconsistency between the models you are comparing will depend on whether the model fits just as well or better/worse in one group than another, and for incremental fit indices like CFI, it will also depend on how poorly the null model fits in each group (or the pooled sample).
